title: Rhizosphere, Endophytes, Mycorrhizae and Microbial Risk

content.overview: Cannabis-associated microbial communities occupy roots, internal tissues and plant surfaces. Some organisms may support plant functions, some may be neutral, and others can be opportunistic pathogens. Microbial management should therefore be evidence-based rather than assuming all inoculation is beneficial.

vocabulary.definition: The soil or media region directly influenced by roots and their exudates.
A microorganism living inside plant tissues without necessarily causing visible disease.
A symbiotic association between certain fungi and plant roots.
The community of microorganisms associated with a defined habitat or host.

sections.title: Plant-associated microbes occupy different niches
sections.body: Cannabis studies identify microbial communities in roots, stems, leaves, flowers and internal tissues. Their location influences how they interact with the plant and how they may be transmitted.

sections.title: Beneficial and harmful roles can coexist
sections.body: Some organisms are investigated for growth promotion or pathogen suppression, while others include potential pathogens. The label microbe does not predict the relationship by itself.

sections.title: Commercial inoculant claims need context
sections.body: Response to introduced organisms can depend on genotype, substrate, existing community and environment. Evidence from one crop or laboratory system should not be presented as a universal cannabis result.

workedExamples: Finding a fungal organism in cannabis tissue does not by itself prove it is beneficial or pathogenic; identify the organism and context before assigning a role.
If an inoculant improves one cultivar in one substrate, treat that result as context-specific until repeated more broadly.
commonMistakes: Ignoring pathogen risk when reusing biological media.
content.practicalApplication: Record substrate, inoculants, sanitation history and crop response. When evaluating a microbial product, identify the organism, claimed mechanism, evidence crop/system and measurable outcome rather than relying on broad microbiome marketing.
content.summary: Cannabis microbiomes are diverse and context dependent. Responsible soil biology distinguishes microbial presence from proven function and beneficial claims from pathogen risk.
